quizData.question: Which of the following is a fundamental rule regarding the basic syntax of Java concerning executable code?
quizData.answer: Every line of executable code must live inside a class.
choices: Every line of executable code must live inside a class.
Executable code must be placed outside of classes to be public.
Variables can be declared without data types if they are executable.
Code blocks are defined by parentheses instead of curly braces.

quizData.question: What are the valid characters and rules for Java identifiers according to language conventions?
quizData.answer: They can contain letters, digits, underscores, and dollar signs, but must not start with a digit or be a reserved keyword.
choices: They can contain letters, digits, underscores, and dollar signs, but must not start with a digit or be a reserved keyword.
They can start with digits as long as they contain no special characters.
They are case-insensitive, meaning 'number' and 'NUMBER' refer to the same variable.
They can include spaces as long as they are enclosed in quotation marks.

What is the difference between Widening Conversion (implicit casting) and Narrowing Conversion (explicit casting) in Java?
quizData.answer: Widening automatically converts a lower precision type to a higher precision type with no loss of information, whereas Narrowing converts higher precision to lower precision and requires an explicit cast.
choices: Widening automatically converts a lower precision type to a higher precision type with no loss of information, whereas Narrowing converts higher precision to lower precision and requires an explicit cast.
Widening requires the `(type)` cast operator, whereas Narrowing happens automatically.
Narrowing is only used for objects, while Widening is only used for primitives.
Widening causes data loss, while Narrowing preserves all precision.
